qt: to the Commission Daniel Buda (PPE) Subject:

The escalation of Russian attacks in the Black Sea is affecting the security of commercial shipping and driving up grain transport and insurance costs, threatening the competitiveness of European agricultural exports through the port of Constanța. Meanwhile, Romania, Bulgaria and Türkiye have agreed on the establishment of a joint mechanism to protect shipping, based on information sharing, monitoring and early-warning systems. These challenges are amplified by international competition, in particular by rising wheat exports from Russia, Argentina and Australia, which are putting additional pressure on prices and European farmers’ income. In view of the above, what specific measures does the European Commission have in mind to: 1.
Support grain exports through the port of Constanța, including by reducing the impact of increased transport and insurance costs due to insecurity in the Black Sea?
Facilitate cooperation between Romania, Bulgaria and Türkiye on protecting commercial shipping, port infrastructure and the continuity of agricultural exports?

Protect the income and competitiveness of European farmers in view of the pressure on global grain prices, including by reducing production costs, diversifying export markets and ensuring a level playing field and compliance with European standards for imports?
